If all entries are non-objects (e.g. [\"bypass\"]), neither branch fires. All three deny rules gate on scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload, so they never fire. scp_r_002_test.rego:46-49 explicitly tests and documents this escape: input_value := [\"not-a-waiver\"] expects 0 results. This means a waivers.json of [\"any-string\"] or [null] passes with zero findings.","impact":"A hostile or careless developer commits waivers.json containing only scalar entries. SCP-R-002 emits no violations. The waiver-consumption layer may reject the file at runtime, but the Rego gate that was intended to protect waiver integrity is silently bypassed. Expired or fake approvals can therefore propagate undetected through the summary artifact.","mitigation":"Add a fourth deny branch that does not require scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload: fire when input is a non-empty array and some entry is not an object. Example: deny contains {\"msg\": msg, \"rule_id\": scp_r_002_rule_id, \"file\": \"output/findings/waivers.json\", \"remediation_url\": scp_r_002_remediation_url} if { is_array(input); count(input) > 0; some index, entry in input; not is_object(entry); msg := sprintf(\"waiver entry %d must be an object\", [index]) }. Remove the scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload guard from this branch. Also add a test that exercises a mixed array (some objects, some scalars) to confirm the new branch fires."},{"id":"SAFETY-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"Break-glass bypass gate references schemas/waivers-file.schema.json which does not exist, making the break-glass path permanently inoperable","evidence":"policy-check.yml:465 — schema_path = Path(\"schemas/waivers-file.schema.json\"). The file listing contains only schemas/waiver.schema.json (singular, not waivers-file). The script explicitly raises FileNotFoundError when schema_path.is_file() is False (line 466: raise FileNotFoundError(schema_path)), which triggers the except block and exits 1. Every invocation of the workflow with scp_bypass=true will fail at this step with SCP-E004.","impact":"The break-glass bypass mechanism is completely inoperable. In a real incident requiring an emergency bypass, teams cannot use the sanctioned path. This creates pressure to remove or skip the CI gate entirely — the opposite of the intended safety property. The waivers schema validation is also never applied in normal runs (bypass gate is skipped when scp_bypass=false), so the only place schema enforcement occurs is permanently broken.","mitigation":"Rename schemas/waiver.schema.json to schemas/waivers-file.schema.json (updating all references, including SCP-R-002's remediation_url), OR correct the path reference in policy-check.yml:465 to schemas/waiver.schema.json. Prefer the latter to avoid breaking SCP-R-002's remediation_url. Add a self-test that verifies the schema file path is resolvable."},{"id":"SAFETY-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"SCP-R-002 omits the required reason field, creating schema drift from waiver.schema.json and allowing reason-free waivers to pass the Rego gate","evidence":"SCP-R-002.rego:9-13 — scp_r_002_required_keys := {\"approved_by\", \"created_at\", \"expires_at\"}. schemas/waiver.schema.json:5-9 — required: [\"reason\", \"approved_by\", \"expires_at\", \"created_at\"]. The reason field is required by the JSON schema but absent from the Rego required-key set. Because the jsonschema validation in the bypass gate only runs when scp_bypass=true (and that gate is broken per SAFETY-002), reason-free waivers pass in all normal workflow runs.","impact":"Waivers without human-readable justification can be committed and consumed. The audit trail for why a policy violation was waived is lost. Since the SCP waiver records are the authoritative approval trail for governance reviews, this degrades the integrity of the D-NNN decision record.","mitigation":"Add \"reason\" to scp_r_002_required_keys. Update the deny fixture (testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/waivers.json) to omit reason to verify the new check fires. Update the allow fixture to include reason."},{"id":"SAFETY-004","severity":"MAJ","claim":"Neither SCP-R-001 nor SCP-R-002 enforce date validity or futurity — expired waivers and past-due deprecation close dates pass indefinitely","evidence":"SCP-R-002.rego:68-72 — scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string checks only that expires_at is a non-empty string; \"2020-01-01\" or \"not-a-date\" both pass. SCP-R-001.rego:19-22 — scp_r_001_allowed_close_dates is a static set {\"2026-06-30\",\"2026-09-30\"}; after 2026-09-30, a bearer_legacy entry with deprecation_close_date \"2026-09-30\" continues to pass. OPA provides time.now_ns() for runtime date comparison but it is not used.","impact":"After the SVC-003 sunset dates pass, the Rego rule cannot detect that bearer_legacy entries have outlived their approved window. Expired waivers grant permanent bypass of SCP-R-002 without re-approval. This undermines the time-bounded nature of both the bearer_legacy deprecation (D-019/D-021) and individual waivers.","mitigation":"For SCP-R-002: validate expires_at format with regex.match(`^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}`, ...) and use time.parse_rfc3339_ns / time.now_ns() to reject past dates. For SCP-R-001: add a deny branch that fires when bearer_legacy close_date has passed: current_ns := time.now_ns(); close_ns := time.parse_rfc3339_ns(sprintf(\"%sT00:00:00Z\", [close_date])); current_ns > close_ns. Both changes require new test cases using future/past timestamps."},{"id":"SAFETY-005","severity":"MIN","claim":"Regal binary is downloaded and executed without SHA256 pin or Sigstore attestation, unlike OPA and Conftest","evidence":"policy-check.yml:224-226 — curl downloads the Regal binary; chmod +x and regal version smoke-test are the only checks. No SHA256 field for regal exists in scripts/scp-policy-check.lock. Compare with OPA: sha256 verified (line 175-178), then gh attestation verify (line 211). Compare with Conftest: archive SHA256 and binary SHA256 both verified (lines 196-221). REGAL_VERSION is hardcoded in the workflow (line 144) rather than read from .tool-versions.","impact":"A compromised Regal release binary could execute arbitrary code in the CI runner. While Regal only reads policy files, a malicious binary could exfiltrate secrets, modify the runner environment, or tamper with output artifacts before the summary step. The risk is amplified because Regal runs with full access to the checked-out repository.","mitigation":"Add regal SHA256 pins to scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for linux-x64 and linux-arm64. Move REGAL_VERSION to scripts/.tool-versions. Apply verify_sha256 after download. Consider adding Sigstore verification when Regal publishes attestations."},{"id":"SAFETY-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"Workflow runs regal lint before opa fmt --fail, inverting the order specified in policies/README.md step 6","evidence":"policy-check.yml:339 — step 'Lint policies with Regal' runs first. policy-check.yml:353 — step 'Check policy formatting with OPA' runs second. policies/README.md:60 — step 6 specifies: 'Run opa fmt --fail policies/', then 'regal lint ...', then 'opa test'. The dispatch-package.json instruction review task explicitly names 'workflow regal+opa fmt step ordering' as a verification item.","impact":"A syntactically malformed Rego file that would fail opa fmt is first fed to Regal. Regal may produce confusing or misleading errors on malformatted Rego, masking the root formatting issue. Contributors following the README would run checks in the correct order locally but see a different order in CI, creating friction and potential for misinterpretation of CI failures.","mitigation":"Swap the step order in policy-check.yml: run 'Check policy formatting with OPA' (opa fmt --fail) before 'Lint policies with Regal', matching the README sequence."},{"id":"SAFETY-007","severity":"MIN","claim":"SCP-R-003 JSON boolean attestation regex does not require a word boundary after 'true', allowing spurious matches like 'true_extra'","evidence":"SCP-R-003.rego:43-44 — regex `(?s).*\"scp:vendoring-attested\"\\s*:\\s*true.*` — the pattern requires 'true' followed by '.*'. Content like '{\"scp:vendoring-attested\": truenotreally}' matches because 'true' is present as a substring before the next '.*'. While a JSON-aware tool would reject this, the Rego rule operates on raw strings and cannot distinguish. policies/** @jrnb2024 present and correct. Adjacent critical files (schemas/, workflow) unprotected (SAFETY-011, nit).

ac_map.ac: AC-8: regal lint + opa fmt --fail steps before conftest invocation
ac_map.note: Both steps present and before policy check invocation. GAPS: step order is regal-first then opa-fmt, inverting README sequence (SAFETY-006); Regal lacks SHA256 pin (SAFETY-005).

findings.claim: scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload detection allows any-non-object array to silently pass waiver validation, enabling wholesale bypass of SCP-R-002
findings.evidence: SCP-R-002.rego:55-66 — scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload is true only when (a) array is empty, or (b) at least one entry is an object with a known key. If all entries are non-objects (e.g. ["bypass"]), neither branch fires. All three deny rules gate on scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload, so they never fire. scp_r_002_test.rego:46-49 explicitly tests and documents this escape: input_value := ["not-a-waiver"] expects 0 results. This means a waivers.json of ["any-string"] or [null] passes with zero findings.
findings.impact: A hostile or careless developer commits waivers.json containing only scalar entries. SCP-R-002 emits no violations. The waiver-consumption layer may reject the file at runtime, but the Rego gate that was intended to protect waiver integrity is silently bypassed. Expired or fake approvals can therefore propagate undetected through the summary artifact.
findings.mitigation: Add a fourth deny branch that does not require scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload: fire when input is a non-empty array and some entry is not an object. Example: deny contains {"msg": msg, "rule_id": scp_r_002_rule_id, "file": "output/findings/waivers.json", "remediation_url": scp_r_002_remediation_url} if { is_array(input); count(input) > 0; some index, entry in input; not is_object(entry); msg := sprintf("waiver entry %d must be an object", [index]) }. Remove the scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload guard from this branch. Also add a test that exercises a mixed array (some objects, some scalars) to confirm the new branch fires.

findings.claim: Break-glass bypass gate references schemas/waivers-file.schema.json which does not exist, making the break-glass path permanently inoperable
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:465 — schema_path = Path("schemas/waivers-file.schema.json"). The file listing contains only schemas/waiver.schema.json (singular, not waivers-file). The script explicitly raises FileNotFoundError when schema_path.is_file() is False (line 466: raise FileNotFoundError(schema_path)), which triggers the except block and exits 1. Every invocation of the workflow with scp_bypass=true will fail at this step with SCP-E004.
findings.impact: The break-glass bypass mechanism is completely inoperable. In a real incident requiring an emergency bypass, teams cannot use the sanctioned path. This creates pressure to remove or skip the CI gate entirely — the opposite of the intended safety property. The waivers schema validation is also never applied in normal runs (bypass gate is skipped when scp_bypass=false), so the only place schema enforcement occurs is permanently broken.
findings.mitigation: Rename schemas/waiver.schema.json to schemas/waivers-file.schema.json (updating all references, including SCP-R-002's remediation_url), OR correct the path reference in policy-check.yml:465 to schemas/waiver.schema.json. Prefer the latter to avoid breaking SCP-R-002's remediation_url. Add a self-test that verifies the schema file path is resolvable.

findings.claim: SCP-R-002 omits the required reason field, creating schema drift from waiver.schema.json and allowing reason-free waivers to pass the Rego gate
findings.evidence: SCP-R-002.rego:9-13 — scp_r_002_required_keys := {"approved_by", "created_at", "expires_at"}. schemas/waiver.schema.json:5-9 — required: ["reason", "approved_by", "expires_at", "created_at"]. The reason field is required by the JSON schema but absent from the Rego required-key set. Because the jsonschema validation in the bypass gate only runs when scp_bypass=true (and that gate is broken per SAFETY-002), reason-free waivers pass in all normal workflow runs.
findings.impact: Waivers without human-readable justification can be committed and consumed. The audit trail for why a policy violation was waived is lost. Since the SCP waiver records are the authoritative approval trail for governance reviews, this degrades the integrity of the D-NNN decision record.
findings.mitigation: Add "reason" to scp_r_002_required_keys. Update the deny fixture (testdata/SCP-R-002/deny/waivers.json) to omit reason to verify the new check fires. Update the allow fixture to include reason.

findings.claim: Neither SCP-R-001 nor SCP-R-002 enforce date validity or futurity — expired waivers and past-due deprecation close dates pass indefinitely
findings.evidence: SCP-R-002.rego:68-72 — scp_r_002_has_nonempty_string checks only that expires_at is a non-empty string; "2020-01-01" or "not-a-date" both pass. SCP-R-001.rego:19-22 — scp_r_001_allowed_close_dates is a static set {"2026-06-30","2026-09-30"}; after 2026-09-30, a bearer_legacy entry with deprecation_close_date "2026-09-30" continues to pass. OPA provides time.now_ns() for runtime date comparison but it is not used.
findings.impact: After the SVC-003 sunset dates pass, the Rego rule cannot detect that bearer_legacy entries have outlived their approved window. Expired waivers grant permanent bypass of SCP-R-002 without re-approval. This undermines the time-bounded nature of both the bearer_legacy deprecation (D-019/D-021) and individual waivers.
findings.mitigation: For SCP-R-002: validate expires_at format with regex.match(`^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}`, ...) and use time.parse_rfc3339_ns / time.now_ns() to reject past dates. For SCP-R-001: add a deny branch that fires when bearer_legacy close_date has passed: current_ns := time.now_ns(); close_ns := time.parse_rfc3339_ns(sprintf("%sT00:00:00Z", [close_date])); current_ns > close_ns. Both changes require new test cases using future/past timestamps.

findings.claim: Regal binary is downloaded and executed without SHA256 pin or Sigstore attestation, unlike OPA and Conftest
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:224-226 — curl downloads the Regal binary; chmod +x and regal version smoke-test are the only checks. No SHA256 field for regal exists in scripts/scp-policy-check.lock. Compare with OPA: sha256 verified (line 175-178), then gh attestation verify (line 211). Compare with Conftest: archive SHA256 and binary SHA256 both verified (lines 196-221). REGAL_VERSION is hardcoded in the workflow (line 144) rather than read from .tool-versions.
findings.impact: A compromised Regal release binary could execute arbitrary code in the CI runner. While Regal only reads policy files, a malicious binary could exfiltrate secrets, modify the runner environment, or tamper with output artifacts before the summary step. The risk is amplified because Regal runs with full access to the checked-out repository.
findings.mitigation: Add regal SHA256 pins to scripts/scp-policy-check.lock for linux-x64 and linux-arm64. Move REGAL_VERSION to scripts/.tool-versions. Apply verify_sha256 after download. Consider adding Sigstore verification when Regal publishes attestations.

findings.claim: Workflow runs regal lint before opa fmt --fail, inverting the order specified in policies/README.md step 6
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:339 — step 'Lint policies with Regal' runs first. policy-check.yml:353 — step 'Check policy formatting with OPA' runs second. policies/README.md:60 — step 6 specifies: 'Run opa fmt --fail policies/', then 'regal lint ...', then 'opa test'. The dispatch-package.json instruction review task explicitly names 'workflow regal+opa fmt step ordering' as a verification item.
findings.impact: A syntactically malformed Rego file that would fail opa fmt is first fed to Regal. Regal may produce confusing or misleading errors on malformatted Rego, masking the root formatting issue. Contributors following the README would run checks in the correct order locally but see a different order in CI, creating friction and potential for misinterpretation of CI failures.
findings.mitigation: Swap the step order in policy-check.yml: run 'Check policy formatting with OPA' (opa fmt --fail) before 'Lint policies with Regal', matching the README sequence.

findings.claim: SCP-R-003 JSON boolean attestation regex does not require a word boundary after 'true', allowing spurious matches like 'true_extra'
findings.evidence: SCP-R-003.rego:43-44 — regex `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true.*` — the pattern requires 'true' followed by '.*'. Content like '{"scp:vendoring-attested": truenotreally}' matches because 'true' is present as a substring before the next '.*'. In a raw-string content field, the Rego rule does not parse JSON — it applies the regex directly to the file content string.
findings.impact: A package.json with a malformed value e.g. 'true_custom' would pass the attestation check even though it is not valid JSON boolean true. While a JSON-aware tool would reject this, the Rego rule operates on raw strings and cannot distinguish. Low probability but represents a technical bypass.
findings.mitigation: Tighten the regex to require a word boundary or non-word character after 'true': `(?s).*"scp:vendoring-attested"\s*:\s*true[^a-zA-Z0-9_].*` or use `true\b`. Add a test case where content contains 'truenotreally' and verify it fires a deny.

findings.claim: SCP-R-001 deny fixture only exercises the runtime_contract.auth_contract.accepted_modes path; the flat services.<name>.auth path has no deny fixture
findings.evidence: policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/services.yml contains only the runtime_contract nesting. scp_r_001_mode_records has two definitions: lines 68-89 (runtime_contract path) and lines 91-101 (flat services.<name>.auth path). scp_r_001_test.rego:25-28 covers the allow case for flat auth (mode.api_key) but no deny test or fixture for flat auth with an invalid mode exists.
findings.impact: A regression in the scp_r_001_mode_records flat-auth definition (e.g., accidental removal or condition change) would not be caught by any fixture. Services using the simplified auth shape (services.<name>.auth.mode) would be silently unvalidated.
findings.mitigation: Add policies/testdata/SCP-R-001/deny/flat_auth/services.yml with content: services: {api: {auth: {mode: "mode.invalid"}}} and add a test test_scp_r_001_denies_invalid_mode_in_flat_auth_shape.

findings.claim: SCP-R-003 deny fixtures are missing for package.json and pyproject.toml without attestation markers
findings.evidence: policies/testdata/SCP-R-003/deny/ contains only go_mod/input.yml. No deny fixture exists for package.json without the boolean marker or pyproject.toml without the comment marker. The test file exercises the deny path only for go.mod (scp_r_003_test.rego:31-41). The allow fixtures exercise package.json with boolean marker and pyproject.toml with comment marker, but their negatives (deny) are untested via fixtures.
findings.impact: Regressions in the attestation-check logic specific to package.json (JSON boolean path) or pyproject.toml (comment path) would not be caught by fixture-based testing. Since these are the two most common manifest types, this is a meaningful gap.
findings.mitigation: Add policies/testdata/SCP-R-003/deny/package_json/input.yml with content lacking the attestation marker, and policies/testdata/SCP-R-003/deny/pyproject_toml/input.yml similarly. Add corresponding test cases.

findings.claim: README rule template uses unprefixed variable names (rule_id, remediation_url) inconsistent with the scp_r_NNN_ prefix convention used by all three implemented rules
findings.evidence: policies/README.md:16-17 — template shows 'rule_id := "SCP-R-NNN"' and 'remediation_url := ...' without prefix. SCP-R-001.rego:5,7 uses scp_r_001_rule_id and scp_r_001_remediation_url. All three rules follow this prefixed pattern. With package main shared across all rules, two rules defining unprefixed rule_id would conflict at evaluation time.
findings.impact: A contributor copying the template verbatim and adding a second rule would create a naming collision, causing OPA to produce an indeterminate/duplicate definition error. The error would be caught at opa test time, not silently, but the template is actively misleading.
findings.mitigation: Update the README template to use scp_r_NNN_rule_id and scp_r_NNN_remediation_url as variable names, matching the established convention.

findings.claim: CODEOWNERS covers only policies/** — schemas/ and .github/workflows/policy-check.yml are unprotected
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS:1 — 'policies/** @jrnb2024'. schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json and schemas/waiver.schema.json are not listed. .github/workflows/policy-check.yml is not listed. A developer could weaken the summary schema (e.g., remove required fields) or modify the workflow step logic without triggering the CODEOWNERS review gate.
findings.impact: The integrity of the policy enforcement pipeline depends equally on the schema contracts and the workflow. Without CODEOWNERS protection, these files can be modified without the governance review that protects the policy files themselves.

findings.claim: scp_r_002_is_waiver_payload empty-array branch (count(input) == 0) is not explicitly tested, risking coverage below 90% threshold
findings.evidence: scp_r_002_test.rego — no test passes input_value := []. The four tests use: a 1-entry valid array, a 1-entry valid array (finding_id variant), a 1-entry invalid array, and a non-object-entry array. The count(input) == 0 branch at SCP-R-002.rego:55-58 is never exercised. OPA coverage tracking counts rule bodies; this untested branch may push SCP-R-002 below the AC-5 90% threshold.
findings.impact: Potential AC-5 violation for SCP-R-002 at the opa test --coverage step; CI may report coverage below threshold, blocking merge.
findings.mitigation: Add test_scp_r_002_allows_empty_waiver_array with input_value := [] expecting count(scp_r_002_results(input_value)) == 0.

structured_review.summary: Slice 020C is NOT at fixpoint. Four MAJ findings block merge: (SAFETY-001) SCP-R-002 non-object array bypass silently passes waiver validation; (SAFETY-002) break-glass schema path references a non-existent file making scp_bypass=true permanently broken; (SAFETY-003) reason field omitted from SCP-R-002 required-key set, schema drift from waiver.schema.json; (SAFETY-004) no date-validity or futurity checks on expires_at/deprecation_close_date, enabling perpetual bypass past sunset dates. Four MIN findings should be resolved before re-dispatch: Regal binary lacks SHA256 pin (supply-chain), regal/opa-fmt step order inverted, R-003 JSON boolean regex lacks word boundary, fixture gaps for R-001 flat-auth deny and R-003 package.json/pyproject.toml deny. Two nits: README template variable naming and CODEOWNERS scope. No CRIT findings.
